descriptionChirho: An interrogative pronoun asking about the quantity, extent, or degree of something uncountable or singular; 'how great' or 'how much.' Used in rhetorical questions about comparative degree (Mt 7:11; 10:25; 12:12; Lk 11:13; 12:24,28; Rom 11:12,24; Phm 1:16; Heb 9:14; 10:29). Translations render as quantity/degree: eng 'how much,' spa 'cuánto/cuánta' (how much), arb كَمْ/فَكَمْ (kam, how much), hin कितना/कितने (kitna, how much), kor 얼마나 더 (eolmana deo, how much more), swa 'zaidi kadiri gani' (to what extent more).

An interrogative pronoun asking about the number of countable items; 'how many.' Used to inquire about discrete quantities such as loaves (Mt 15:34; 16:9-10; Mk 6:38; 8:5,19-20), years (Lk 15:17; Mk 15:4), or workers (Lk 15:17). Translations shift to countable forms: eng 'how many,' spa 'cuántas/cuántos' (how many, feminine/masculine plural), arb كَمْ (kam, how many), hin कितनी/कितनि (kitni, how many), kor 몇 (myeot, how many/several), swa 'mingapi' (how many). The plural morphology of the pronoun itself marks the countable distinction from the singular 'how much.'
